This page sweeps the inductor of the pad resonator of
[Resonant modes with Palace](modes-palace.qmd) through 10, 12 and 14 nH in
HFSS Eigenmode. Each of the three models is built and saved on a workstation
with AEDT, the three are solved one after another on an HPC computer with
AEDT's command-line solver and no desktop, and the results come back to the
workstation, which reads each model's frequency, Q and energy participations.
The procedure has not been run end to end with AEDT, and this repository
holds no result of it.

[]{#hosts-and-prerequisites}Three computers, or three sessions, take part:

| Stage | Where | What it needs |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Build and package each model | Workstation | SCGSim with its `aedt-epr` extra and the OrcaPen SC PDK, AEDT 2024.2 with its desktop and licence |
| 2. Solve | HPC computer | AEDT 2024.2's command-line solver and licence, and Python 3.12; no SCGSim, no PyAEDT, no desktop |
| 3. Collect | Workstation | The same as stage 1 |

Use the same AEDT release on all three.

## 1. Build and package each model {#prepare-and-package-each-model}

Set `AEDT_BATCH_EXECUTABLE` to the AEDT executable as it is called on the HPC
computer; it is written into each package and run there. Then run this script
on the workstation, in a new study folder:

```python
import json
import os
import subprocess
import tarfile
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import gdsfactory as gf
import orcapen_sc_pdk
from orcapen_sc_pdk import get_material_records
from orcapen_sc_pdk.tech import get_single_die_layer_stack
from scgsim.aedt import (
    AedtResources, EigenmodeRunControl, EigenmodeSim, EprAnalysisRequest,
    planar_junction_from_port, prepare_native_batch,
)
from scgsim.geometry import GeometryPlan, JunctionTerminalBinding, RectangularJunctionSpec

# The pad of First simulation, with its junction sheet declared as a junction.
orcapen_sc_pdk.activate()
component = gf.get_component(
    "square_pad_capacitor", pad_side_um=200.0, gap_um=20.0, die_side_um=1000.0
)
plan = GeometryPlan(
    component=component,
    root_id="chip",
    layer_stack=get_single_die_layer_stack(),
    material_records=get_material_records(),
    coupon_padding_um=0.0,
)
plan.set_nets({"pad": ("chip/PAD",), "ground": ("chip/GROUND",)})
plan.set_vacuum_region(padding=(0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
plan.set_rectangular_junctions([
    RectangularJunctionSpec(
        junction_id="jj",
        port_sheet_id="PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__0000",
        source_polygon_id="PORT_SHEET__chip/o_junction_lumped__SOURCE__P0000",
        source_occurrence_path="chip",
        terminal_a=JunctionTerminalBinding("chip/PAD", "chip", "pad"),
        terminal_b=JunctionTerminalBinding("chip/GROUND", "chip", "ground"),
    )
])
snapshot = plan.prepare()
junction = planar_junction_from_port(
    snapshot.geometry_input,
    port_name="chip/o_junction_lumped",
    junction_id="jj",
    terminal_a_net="pad",
    terminal_b_net="ground",
    inductance_h=10e-9,
    capacitance_f=0.0,
)

AEDT_VERSION = "2024.2"  # The same release on all three computers.
resources = AedtResources(cores=4, ram_limit_percent=80)
study = (Path.cwd() / ".artifacts" / "pad-hpc-sweep").resolve()
packages = study / "packages"
packages.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
rows = []
for case_id, inductance_h in (("L10nH", 10e-9), ("L12nH", 12e-9), ("L14nH", 14e-9)):
    sim = EigenmodeSim(modeling="solid", aedt_version=AEDT_VERSION)
    sim.set_plan(snapshot)
    sim.set_output_dir(study / "prepared" / case_id)
    sim.set_eigenmode(
        project_name=f"pad_{case_id}",
        design_name="PadLC",
        run_control=EigenmodeRunControl(
            setup_name="Setup1", minimum_frequency_ghz=3.0, num_modes=1,
            maximum_passes=20, maximum_delta_frequency_percent=0.1,
            minimum_passes=1, minimum_converged_passes=1,
        ),
        resources=resources,
    )
    sim.add_junction(replace(junction, inductance_h=inductance_h))
    sim.set_epr_request(EprAnalysisRequest(
        mode_indices=(1,),
        surface_epr_groups=None,  # every Surface EPR group of the plan (none here)
        junction_ids=("jj",),
        bulk_domain_ids=None,  # every dielectric solid and the Region
    ))
    handoff = sim.prepare_handoff()  # Writes the run folder; opens no AEDT.
    subprocess.run(["bash", str(handoff.script_path), "--prepare-only"], check=True)
    package = prepare_native_batch(
        handoff.run_dir,
        output_dir=packages / case_id,
        solver_executable=os.environ["AEDT_BATCH_EXECUTABLE"],
        resources=resources,
    )
    rows.append({
        "case_id": case_id,
        "inductance_h": inductance_h,
        "package": package.root.relative_to(study).as_posix(),
    })

manifest = study / "sweep.json"
manifest.write_text(json.dumps({"aedt_version": AEDT_VERSION, "cases": rows}, indent=2) + "\n")
outbound = study / "pad-sweep-inputs.tar.gz"
with tarfile.open(outbound, "w:gz") as archive:
    archive.add(manifest, arcname="sweep.json")
    archive.add(packages, arcname="packages")
print(outbound)
```

For each inductance, the loop:

1. prepares a run folder with `prepare_handoff()`, as [Resonant modes with
   HFSS](modes-hfss.qmd) does, here with an EPR request for the junction and
   the dielectrics;
2. runs that folder's `run_aedt.sh --prepare-only`: AEDT builds the model,
   sets up the solve and the EPR calculations, saves the project and closes,
   without solving;
3. packages the saved project for the HPC solver with
   `prepare_native_batch()`.

The junction needs `plan.set_rectangular_junctions` before `prepare()`: it
names the junction sheet and the pad and ground Entities it joins, pad first,
because the sheet's direction points from the pad to the ground. Only the
inductance changes between the models, so one plan serves all three; a sweep
of the geometry needs a new plan, snapshot and junction for each case.
`sweep.json` is your own table of cases; SCGSim has no sweep function.

Each `packages/<case>` holds `native-batch-package.json`, `run_batch.py` and
`native_batch.tar.gz`. Keep the `prepared/` folders on the workstation.

## 2. Solve on HPC {#transfer-one-archive-and-solve-serially-on-hpc}

Copy `pad-sweep-inputs.tar.gz` to the HPC computer. In a new working folder
there, run this with Python 3.12 alone:

```python
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
from pathlib import Path

incoming = Path("pad-sweep-inputs.tar.gz").resolve()
workspace = (Path.cwd() / "pad-hpc-run").resolve()
workspace.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
with tarfile.open(incoming, "r:gz") as archive:
    archive.extractall(workspace, filter="data")
sweep = json.loads((workspace / "sweep.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
attempts = workspace / "attempts"
attempts.mkdir()
for row in sweep["cases"]:
    package_dir = workspace / row["package"]
    subprocess.run([
        sys.executable, str(package_dir / "run_batch.py"), "solve",
        "--package", str(package_dir),
        "--output", str(attempts / row["case_id"]),
    ], check=True)

returned = workspace.parent / "pad-sweep-returned.tar.gz"
with tarfile.open(returned, "x:gz") as archive:
    for name in ("sweep.json", "packages", "attempts"):
        archive.add(workspace / name, arcname=name)
print(returned)
```

`run_batch.py solve` runs AEDT's batch solve on the packaged project with the
packaged resources, on this one computer; it submits no scheduler job. To use
your site's scheduler, run one case per job instead of the loop. Each
attempt keeps `batch-attempt.json`, the solver's output and its complete
`work/` folder. If a case fails, the loop stops and keeps that attempt and its
logs; it does not run the case again.

## 3. Collect the results {#return-all-attempts-and-collect-full-epr}

Copy `pad-sweep-returned.tar.gz` back to the workstation, whole: the
adaptive history and the saved fields are in the returned project's
`.aedtresults` folder. Then run, in the SCGSim environment:

```python
import json
import tarfile
from pathlib import Path

from scgsim.aedt import collect_native_batch

incoming = Path("pad-sweep-returned.tar.gz").resolve()
returned_root = (Path.cwd() / "pad-returned").resolve()
returned_root.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
with tarfile.open(incoming, "r:gz") as archive:
    archive.extractall(returned_root, filter="data")
sweep = json.loads((returned_root / "sweep.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
collected_root = (Path.cwd() / "pad-collected").resolve()
collected_root.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
for row in sweep["cases"]:
    run = collect_native_batch(
        returned_root / row["package"],
        returned_root / "attempts" / row["case_id"],
        output_dir=collected_root / row["case_id"],
    )
    print(row["case_id"], "L =", row["inductance_h"], "H")
    print(run.physics_results())
    print(run.epr_result())
```

`collect_native_batch()` opens a copy of each returned project in AEDT, reads
the adaptive history and the EPR of the saved fields, and returns the result
as `resolve_results()` would, without solving again or rebuilding the model.
`physics_results()` gives the mode's `frequency_ghz` and `q_factor`, and
`epr_result()` the participations. A case whose history or saved fields are
missing fails here and keeps its output for diagnosis.

## Comparing the cases {#read-version-and-stage-records}

Only the inductance changes between the three cases: the geometry, the
materials, the EPR request and the solver controls are the same. Compare each
case's frequency with its own convergence status and history, as
[Convergence and reports](convergence-and-reports.qmd#interpret-for-scq-use)
describes. The report of each case also records the AEDT release used at each
stage. The [batch reference](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#prepared-native-hfss-epr-batch)
gives the package contents and every failure rule.
